analysis:
Integration reviewed the batch analyses against the replayed production patch in SSDWholeRootMaintainer.swift. The change adds a per-root readableHeaderIdentities map, guarded by maintenanceLock. It records the lstat identity (dev, ino, size, mtime ns, ctime ns) of block files whose DBK3 header read succeeded. A later pass skips readMetadataOnly only if the identity is unchanged and fanoutPassesReadChecks(fanout) holds. That check reruns isSafeModelRoot, pathResolvesToItself, isRealDirectory and the no-follow SSDNoFollowIO.openDirectoryChain walk. Reasons no regression was found against T-041 (TB-007, A-001):
- The identity is read before the header read, so a concurrent change is re-read next pass.
- Failures are never cached, so a transient EIO or EMFILE cannot keep an owned block past its TTL. The defer replaces the map with only the current readable set, so deleted files are pruned and growth is bounded by the file count.
- A content write or rename changes ctime or inode. A same-UID attacker can restore mtime but not ctime, and the operator already controls the machine under TB-003.
- The symlink and regular-file guards before the header check are unchanged, as are TTL (1800 s), budget, HMAC naming, AES-GCM authentication and removal paths.
- The new tests (remembersHeaderVerdictsOnlyForUnchangedFiles, replacedLookalikeIsReadAgain, failedHeaderReadIsRetried) pin ctime invalidation, lookalike re-read and retry after a failed read.
- The docs and changelog match the code.
Residual unverified items, none of them evidence of a defect:
- The call site was not seen, so I could not confirm that scan access to the map is always under maintenanceLock.
- The SSDBlockStore helper implementations were not supplied.
- Downstream consumption of metadataReadable was not checked.
A forged-stat controller on an external volume is already outside the accepted boundary in T-041. Test-only units introduce no attack surface.
